history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: seq 2352 is the SAME famous Matabari Shakti Peetha already documented as seq 1021 (id tripura-sundari-temple-matabari-udaipur) and seq 1026 (id tripureshwari-temple-matabari-udaipur) - recommend merging all three into one canonical record. Identity confirmed: this is the renowned Tripura Sundari Temple, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas (legend: Sati's right foot fell here; her Bhairava is Tripuresh), the shrine that gave Tripura its name. Built in 1501 CE by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya after a divine dream; the hilltop already held a Vishnu shrine, and the king reconciled the vision as the unity of Vishnu and Shakti. Bengali Ek-ratna style: square sanctum with a conical/pagoda-like dome, on a tortoise-hump-shaped hillock (Kurma Pith). The 5-ft Tripura Sundari idol was brought from Chittagong; a smaller 2-ft 'Chhota Ma' (Chandi) stands beside her. Behind the temple lies the Kalyan Sagar lake, home to rare, revered Bostami turtles. Second-most-visited temple in Northeast India after Kamakhya. Redeveloped under the PRASHAD scheme (Rs 34.43 crore), inaugurated by PM Modi on 22 September 2025.

name: Tripura Sundari Temple (Matabari)
town: Matabari, Udaipur (CSV town 'Udaipur' correct; the temple stands at Matabari, ~5 km from Udaipur town)
town_description: Udaipur (ancient Rangamati) in Gomati district was the capital of the Tripura kingdom under the Manikya dynasty before the capital shifted to Agartala. The Tripura Sundari Temple stands on a small hillock at Matabari on the south-western outskirts of Udaipur town, about 55 km south of Agartala, and is Tripura's most famous Hindu pilgrimage site.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala, about 55 km by road.
travel.railway: Udaipur (Tripura) railway station is the nearest major railhead; a Matabari rail station is reported about 2 km away (verify).
travel.road: On the Agartala-Sabroom road (NH-8), about 5 km from Udaipur town and 55 km from Agartala; the temple has its own management trust with pilgrim accommodation.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Diwali for the famous mela (expect very large crowds).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: the temple's official listing gives 4:00 AM-10:00 PM daily; other directories list about 5:30/6:00 AM-9:00 PM, some with a midday break (verify on the day of visit).
